newsitem.title: JAPAN: Panic sales knock dlr down vs yen by Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: Panic sales knock dlr down vs yen by Tokyo noon.

text.p: Panic dollar sales by Japanese trust banks and other institutional investors knocked the dollar down by more than one yen by Tokyo noon on Thursday.
The dollar fell as low as 115.70 yen in early trade.
"I would call it a mini dollar-selling climax prompted by panicky dollar selling by Japanese investors for loss cutting and hedging purposes," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
"A major surge of sales would emerge if the dollar slides further and goes below 115 yen," the U.S. bank trader said.
Traders said that Japanese trust banks alone sold a total of more than $1 billion in early trading.

Those sales partly reflected an attempt by the banks to increase currency hedge ratios -- or the volume of forward dollar selling against the total dollar-asset exposure in their inventory. A hedge ratio tends to increase when investors see a greater chance of the dollar falling in the future.
A wave of loss-cut selling emerged when the U.S. currency sank below 116.30-50 yen from an early peak of 117.48 yen.

Meanwhile, Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted by a Japanese news agency as saying that the agreement on currencies by the Group of Seven industrialised nations has "sufficiently" filtered through into the currency market, comments which appeared aimed at preventing a further steep fall in the dollar.
Market speculation that the U.S. Treasury would support a stronger Japanese currency was also behind the dollar's tumble this morning, traders said.

The speculation started in New York on Wednesday, fuelled by market gossip that a newsletter from a Washington-based consulting firm stated that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was calling for an exchange rate of 115 yen per dollar.
But subscribers to the newsletter contacted by Reuters denied having received such a report.
The talk, which hit currency markets in late New York trading, triggered previously set orders to sell dollars for yen. The already ailing dollar had sunk briefly to 116.95 yen overnight.
